title: VRUN: Vaults of Obsolete Code (Game Boy), V4: the whole game (the music placeholders)
description: The user's Game Boy game (docs/projects/vrun-voc-plan.md), milestone V4: the title (MP_VRUN) and its menu (RUN 18 clovers, SHORT RUN 5-8, TUTORIAL 3 on VRUN3, Dashless, OPTIONS, CONTINUE), 32 maps, the dark grid, the box, the suspend save, the clear screen, the real sound effects (V3) and the music engine with placeholder songs (V5); the physics of the original (Eternal Degrade's MP_VirusRun) reproduced tick for tick (tests/physics/compare.ps1, compare_maps.ps1). One dual-mode ROM (MBC5 + RAM + battery, 1 MB, 32 KB). Built with GBDK-2020 4.5.0 (toolchains.json) in its live workspace PROJECTS/VRUN_VOC_dev (its own git, local commits only).

toolchain: GBDK-2020 4.5.0 (lcc, SDCC, sdasgb, sdldgb, makebin), pinned in toolchains.json

steps.name: build
steps.note: build.ps1: lcc -autobank on src, src/maps, src/phys; it checks the cartridge header and that bank 0 does not overflow.

run.note: The title (Left / Right: the mode), then A. Left / Right run, Down brakes, A / B jump (mid-air: freeze, then a direction dashes), Select = the abort lottery, Start = pause.

memory.what: the run is on (the title's A started RUN)
no picture came late: every tick on the screen on its 24 Hz boundary

prints: VRUN: Vaults of Obsolete Code, V4, dev build

scenarios.why: on a Game Boy Color (double speed): the run plays, the pad reaches the physics, no tick late

memory.what: the original Game Boy, the slowest: still no late picture

scenarios.why: the same cartridge on an original Game Boy: four shades, the same game, on time

compat.what: The tutorial on every Game Boy emulator BrokenDev has, from power-on and the same pad script: the run's state read by the game's symbols every frame. The other emulators play their boot animation first, so the pad script waits until frame 400 and the checks allow for the difference.

scenarios.what: power-on, the title, A, a run with a few keys

checks.what: the vblank handler runs (frame_count keeps changing)
the 24 Hz ticks run (tick_count's low byte keeps changing)
the picture changed between the title and the run
BrokenDev hardware checks (D4). One finding is accepted, by design: gb.lag-frame.

accepted.reason: The game ticks at 24 Hz, as the original: a tick's work (its first part and its picture, in the main program and in the vblank handler) spans the 2 or 3 frames of the tick by design, so vblank always arrives in the middle of it. Lateness is measured where it matters, per tick: tick_late (verify's memory check) and the debug port's '@late' (tests/game/speed.ps1), both 0.

budgets.what: Over a limit fails verify, near it (90%) warns.

romBankFree.what: the map banks 33-36 are full by design (146 layouts of 112 bytes each); build.ps1 fails on a bank 0 overflow

memoryFree.what: an original Game Boy's 8 KB of work RAM

knownIssues: The music is the music engine with placeholder songs (converted from the VRUN NES soundtrack) until the user's arrangements (V5).
No hardware test on the user's flash cartridge yet.
